children: Danaher and Microsoft are teaming up to develop an agentic AI platform designed for scientific instruments and laboratories.
Danaher said Friday the partnership aims to help streamline experimental operations and speed up laboratory findings.

The platform will be built on Microsoft's AI technologies using Danaher's scientific, workflow and instrumentation expertise. It will aim to enable reuse and interoperability across technologies, so specialized products can be built on a shared foundation while remaining open to agents and digital solutions in multi-vendor laboratories, Danaher said.

Danaher said that while the platform is still under development, its first commercial AI applications--including an AI assistant designed to provide product support for cellular imaging systems--will reach its customers this year. Additional agent-enabled instruments from Danaher businesses that use the platform are planned for 2027, the company said.

"With Microsoft, we are building a common foundation, so our instruments and laboratories work together consistently, as one connected Danaher," said Julie Sawyer Montgomery, Danaher's president and chief executive.
